items.name: Commit message
items.description: Write a precise conventional commit from a diff or a list of changes.
items.author: JIT

install.body:
---
name: commit-message
title: Commit message
description: Write a precise conventional commit message from a diff or a description of changes.
when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a commit message, wants to commit changes, or needs a changelog-ready summary of a diff.
categories: Engineering, Git
aliases: commit msg, conventional commit, git commit message
---
# Commit message

Turn a change into one commit message that a reviewer can understand without opening the diff.

## Steps

1. Read the diff (`git diff --staged` or the supplied changes). Identify the primary behavior change, not every file that was touched.
2. Choose a Conventional Commits type: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `perf`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, or `chore`.
3. Write the subject in the imperative mood, at most 72 characters, with no trailing period.
4. Add a body only when the reason is not obvious. Wrap at 72 characters. Explain why, not what.
5. Add `BREAKING CHANGE:` when a public contract changes.

## Output

Return one fenced `text` block with the message and nothing else. If the diff contains unrelated changes, say so and propose splitting the commit.

items.name: Release notes
items.description: Draft user-facing release notes from a git log or a version diff.
items.author: JIT

install.body:
---
name: release-notes
title: Release notes
description: Draft release notes from a git log, a list of commits, or a version diff.
when_to_use: Use when preparing a release, writing a changelog, or summarizing what changed between two versions.
categories: Engineering, Releases
aliases: changelog, release summary, what changed
---
# Release notes

Write for the people who use the software, not only for the people who wrote it.

## Steps

1. Collect the changes (`git log v1.2.0..HEAD`, a commit list, or a diff summary).
2. Group them under `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`, `Removed`, and `Security`. Omit empty groups.
3. Lead with user-visible outcomes. Keep internal refactors out unless they affect behavior.
4. Link issues or pull requests when the input includes them.
5. Put breaking changes first, with the migration step.

## Output

Return Markdown. Start with a one-sentence summary, then the grouped bullets. Do not invent changes that are not in the input.

items.name: Bug report
items.description: Turn a stack trace or a vague complaint into a reproducible bug report.
items.author: JIT

install.body:
---
name: bug-report
title: Bug report
description: Turn a stack trace, logs, or a vague complaint into a reproducible bug report.
when_to_use: Use when the user reports a bug, pastes an error, or asks for help filing an issue.
categories: Engineering, Support
aliases: issue report, reproduce a bug, error report
---
# Bug report

Make the failure reproducible before proposing a fix.

## Steps

1. State the expected behavior and the actual behavior in one sentence each.
2. Extract the smallest reproduction: commands, inputs, environment, and version.
3. Include the first relevant error and the stack frames that point at the project, not the framework.
4. List what you already ruled out.
5. Propose one next diagnostic step, not a speculative fix.

## Output

Return Markdown with `Summary`, `Steps to reproduce`, `Expected`, `Actual`, `Environment`, and `Notes`. If a detail is missing, mark it `unknown` rather than guessing.
